ideas.idea: Replace the home page div onClick with a real <Link to="/features">
ideas.why: This is the same as the known problem about /features being reached only by a div, so it adds nothing new, though it is accurate.

ideas.idea: Add real plan names, contents and prices to the pricing page
ideas.why: pricing.tsx says only 'Plans that grow with your team. Talk to us for a quote.' and names no plan, so there is little for people or machines to read.

ideas.idea: Give pricing its own title and description
ideas.why: This repeats the known problem that /pricing has no meta export.

ideas.idea: Name the integrations on the home page, perhaps with a page per integration
ideas.why: The home page says 'Integrates with all the tools you already use' and names none, so listing them gives visitors and machines concrete content.

ideas.idea: Expand the features page with a short explanation and heading per feature
ideas.why: features.tsx has one line of text and a single h1, so the page has very little content to explain.
This is accurate because the sitemap has no dates, but it would apply to almost any site and has a small effect.

ideas.idea: Add internal links between pages and a footer linking all main pages
ideas.why: The home page, features and pricing have no content links to each other and the only links are in the root nav, so a footer and cross-links would help discovery. The claim that the home page links nowhere is slightly overstated because the nav is on every page.

ideas.idea: Add Organization or WebSite JSON-LD in root.tsx
ideas.why: The brief says having no JSON-LD is not a required fix, so recommending it as a gap goes against that.

ideas.idea: Add charset, viewport and Open Graph tags to meta
ideas.why: This is accurate because root.tsx has none of them, but it is standard advice for any site. Viewport and charset matter somewhat, and Open Graph tags matter little for being found.

ideas.idea: Generate sitemap.xml from routes instead of keeping it by hand
ideas.why: This is accurate because the sitemap is a static file, but with four routes the maintenance benefit is small and the advice fits any site.
